note: Long make-X / get-X drill (zahha2, 5awwaf, za33al, da77ak, ta33ab); several of his Arabic attempts are missing from the transcript (29:50-30:31, 27:17). A5 looks like a fact fix (wrong hour), not a clock-time grammar slip.

row.why: He used the fusha form الصباح for 'morning'; Amal recast الصبح (sheet: morning | el-sube7 | الصبح). Her 'على؟' only asked for the hour; 'صحيت بدري الصباح' needs no preposition, so it is not a D1 slip.
row.english: I woke up early in the morning.

rulings.why: Transcript supports the recast of الصباح -> الصبح; the 'على؟' was a request for the time, not a fix of a missing preposition.

S5: 'tabe-tabe-tabu, uh, tabu tu' is a restart chain and the engine's Latin of his last try and her 'Tab tu' differ by one vowel; no 'no', no explanation, she moved straight on - cannot be shown to be a wrong form rather than a stutter.

row.medi_said: أنا بخاف ... Ana bakhaf- ... بكون أخاف؟
row.amal_said: No. It's an adjective ... Ana khayef.
row.why: For 'I am scared' he used the present verb ba5aaf (I get scared); Amal said 'No. It's an adjective' and gave the state word 5aayef - exactly B15 participles (not taught yet: filed, shown, not counted).

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same slip; the fix is verb -> participle, which is the B15 rule itself, so grammar B15 rather than vocab tier 2.

row.medi_said: kan, sorry. Kan, uh, يضحو ... Yadah. Yadah.
row.why: 'The show was funny' needs the make-laugh form yda77ek (sheet: funny | Beyda77ek); he produced يضحو / yadah (get-side / broken form), Amal recast 'Yadahak' and he repeated يضحّك at 20:14. Engine Latin hides the shadda, hence low.

rulings.why: Real voiced recast after a wrong verb form; his kaan was already right (self-fixed كنت -> kan), so the slip is the make-X vs get-X verb (B12), not B7.

Not an error: he restated her prompt as 'I made them scared' (31:24, in English) and then gave a right Arabic form for 'them'; Amal said both khawafatum / khawaftum are right. A misheard English prompt is not a grammar slip.

row.medi_said: lish bit'asabi, bit'asabi lama ihna- ... ma binishrab ahwa.
row.right: لما ما تشربي قهوة (lamma ma teshrabi ahwe)
row.why: Prompt was 'when YOU don't drink coffee'; he said ihna (we) and kept b- after lamma; Amal re-said 'When you don't drink' and he fixed to 'lama inti ma tishrebi ahwa' at 35:10-35:21. Verb matched his own pronoun, so the wrong piece is the pronoun (A12); b- after lamma is B3.
row.english: Why do you get angry when you don't drink coffee?

rulings.why: Her English prompt targets the person; his verb agreed with ihna, so A12 (pronoun for the real person) fits better than B18; the b- he also dropped is B3.

row.medi_said: So do we only say bizaghe because there's no adjective for bizaghe?
row.amal_said: We have mumil, but we chose not to learn it before. Mumil.
row.why: Didn't-know: he asked whether there is an adjective for 'boring'; Amal supplied mumil (sheet: boring | Mumell | ممل).

rulings.why: Amal supplied a word in answer to his question - a didn't-know, tier 0, as the brief defines.

row.medi_said: They upset me. My par... Upset me. (engine dropped his Arabic)
row.amal_said: You're looking for the verb ... But I want the other one. [laughs]
row.why: For 'my parents made me upset' Amal steered him off the adjective to the verb, then said 'But I want the other one' - he gave the wrong side of the za3al / za33al pair; his Arabic is missing from the transcript, so low.

rulings.why: Her 'I want the other one' after his attempt is a voiced no on the make/get side; kept low because the transcript dropped his Arabic.

challenges.why: الساعة تلات ... ستة وعشرين is correct E2 form (el-saa3a + feminine number); Amal's تنتين corrects the hour (it was 2:26), a fact fix, not a clock-time grammar slip.
